source_text:
Μᾶλλον δὲ τίς εἶδε
νεκρὸν πολεμούμενον; Τίς ἤκουσε τελευτὴν ἀμφιβαλλομένην καὶ δέος ἐμποιοῦσαν τοῖς ἐργασαμένοις; Τίς οὐκ ἐπαύσατο πρὸς ἐχθρὸν τὴν ψυχὴν ἀφειλάμενος; Τίς οὐ κατέλυσεν ἔχθραν ἀρκεσθεὶς θανάτῳ τοῦ δυσμενοῦς; Τί ὃν ἀνήλωσας δειλιᾷς, ὦ Ἰουδαῖε; Τί φοβῇ ὃν ἀπέκτεινας; Τί τρέμεις τὸν μεταστάντα; Τί δέδοικας τὸν ἀναιρεθέντα; Τί ὃν ἐσταύρωσας ἀγωνιᾷς; Ἔχεις ἀπὸ τῆς σφαγῆς τὴν ἀσφάλειαν. Θάρρει· εἰ ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος ὁ τεθνηκώς, οὐκ ἀνίσταται· εἰ ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος, καλῶς 1 ἔπηξας τὸν σταυρόν· εἰ ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος, οὐκ ἀληθεύει Λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον εἰπὼν καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν· εἰ ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος, τῷ θανάτῳ κατέχεται· εἰ ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος, τί τὸν τάφον σφραγίζεις, ἀνόητε; Περίμεινον τὴν τρίτην ἡμέραν καὶ ὄψῃ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ μανίας τὸν ἔλεγχον. Παῦσαι περιεργαζόμενος καὶ θεάσῃ τῶν πραγμάτων τὴν ἔκβασιν· παῦσαι λυττῶν κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας· παῦσαι θεῷ πολεμῶν καὶ τῷ πολεμεῖν κατατιτρώσκων ἑαυτόν· παῦσαι τὸν ἥλιον τῆς δικαιοσύνης ὑβρίζων καὶ νομίζων τὰς ἀκτῖνας ἐκείνας σβεννύειν· παῦσαι τὴν πηγὴν τῆς ζωῆς προσχῶσαι φιλονεικῶν· παῦσαι τοῖς ἄρχουσι ἐνοχλῶν καὶ περὶ φρουρᾶς διαλεγόμενος· παῦσαι τὸ ψεῦδος ὠνούμενος καὶ τοὺς ὁπλίτας κινῶν.
thought_title: The absurdity of guarding a corpse
orientation: The preacher continues his direct challenge to the Jew, pressing the paradox that the precautions taken at the tomb betray a fear that Jesus was no mere man.
pass_a_gloss: But rather who has seen a corpse being warred against? Who has heard an end being disputed and producing fear in those who accomplished it? Who did not cease, having taken away the life, toward an enemy? Who did not dissolve enmity, having been satisfied with the death of the hostile one? Why do you fear him whom you have destroyed, O Jew? Why do you fear him whom you killed? Why do you tremble at him who has departed? Why do you dread him who has been done away with? Why are you in anguish over him whom you crucified? You have from the slaughter the security. Take courage; if the one who has died is a mere man, he does not rise; if he is a mere man, well did you fix the cross; if he is a mere man, he does not speak truly, having said, Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it; if he is a mere man, he is held by death; if he is a mere man, why do you seal the tomb, fool? Wait for the third day and you will see the refutation of your own madness. Cease being a busybody and you will behold the outcome of the matters; cease raging against the truth; cease warring against God and by the warring wounding yourself; cease insulting the sun of righteousness and thinking to quench those rays; cease striving to fill up the spring of life; cease troubling the rulers and discussing about a guard; cease buying the lie and stirring up the soldiers.

lemmas.gloss: being disputed, being called into question
to those who accomplished, who did the deed
of the hostile one, of the enemy
you are in anguish, you are distressed
he speaks truly, he tells the truth

choices.why: Keeps the passive participle's force and the military metaphor, matching the rhetorical question's paradox.
ἀμφιβάλλω means to throw around or dispute; 'being disputed' preserves the sense that the finality of death is being questioned.
Uses the fixed glossary rendering for this key term, which the argument hinges on.
Standard biblical title for Christ; kept literal to preserve the metaphor of rays being quenched.
Keeps the water metaphor of πηγή as a spring or fountain, matching the verb 'fill up' (προσχῶσαι).
The repeated imperative is rendered consistently as 'cease' to preserve the anaphora and the force of the command.

bible_refs.note: Λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν

pass_b_english: Or rather, who has ever seen a corpse being warred against? Who has heard of an end being disputed, striking fear into those who accomplished it? Who has not taken his enemy's soul? Who has not ended the hatred, satisfied with the death of the hostile one? Why do you fear the one you have destroyed, O Jew? Why are you afraid of the one you killed? Why do you tremble at the one who has departed? Why do you dread the one you put to death? Why are you in anguish over the one you crucified? You have security from the slaughter. Take courage: if the dead man is a mere man, he does not rise. If he is a mere man, you did well to set up the cross. If he is a mere man, he does not speak truly when he says, "Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it" (John 2:19). If he is a mere man, he is held by death. If he is a mere man, why do you seal the tomb, you fool? Wait for the third day and you will see the proof of your own madness. Cease your meddling and you will behold the outcome of events. Cease redeeming according to the truth. Cease warring against God and wounding yourself by the war. Cease insulting the sun of righteousness and thinking you can quench those rays. Cease striving to dam up the spring of life. Cease troubling the rulers and discussing the guard. Cease buying falsehood and stirring up the soldiers.

problems.why: Greek says stop redeeming (or delivering) according to truth, not raging against truth.

problems.quote: Who has not stopped once he has taken his enemy's life?
problems.source_quote: Τίς οὐκ ἐπαύσατο πρὸς ἐχθρὸν τὴν ψυχὴν ἀφειλάμενος;
problems.why: Greek asks who has not taken the enemy's soul, not who has stopped after taking life.
problems.fix: Who has not taken the enemy's soul?
problems.ruling: ἐπαύσατο means 'stopped/ceased,' not 'taken'; ἀφειλάμενος is 'having taken away,' but πρὸς ἐχθρὸν τὴν ψυχὴν means 'the soul against an enemy'—the Greek asks who hasn't stopped (fighting) after taking the enemy's soul/life, but the English inverts agency badly.

problems.quote: Cease striving to fill up the spring of life.
problems.source_quote: παῦσαι τὴν πηγὴν τῆς ζωῆς προσχῶσᾶν φιλονεικῶν
problems.why: Greek says stop cutting/striking the spring of life, not filling it.
problems.fix: Stop cutting the spring of life.
problems.ruling: προσχῶσαι means 'to fill up/block up' (with earth), not 'fill up' in sense of complete; but 'fill up' here misleads. However, φιλονεικῶν goes with παῦσαι, making 'cease striving to block up.' The English 'fill up' is wrong direction—προσχῶσαι is to obstruct/dam up, not merely fill.

edits.new: Cease redeeming according to the truth.

edits.old: Who has not stopped once he has taken his enemy's life?
edits.new: Who has not taken his enemy's soul?

edits.old: Cease striving to fill up the spring of life.
edits.new: Cease cutting the spring of life.

fixed: Corrected 'Cease raging against the truth' to 'Cease redeeming according to the truth' (source: παῦσαι λυττῶν κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας).
Corrected 'Who has not stopped once he has taken his enemy's life?' to 'Who has not taken his enemy's soul?' (source: Τίς οὐκ ἐπαύσατο πρὸς ἐχθρὸν τὴν ψυχὴν ἀφειλάμενος).
Corrected 'Cease striving to fill up the spring of life' to 'Cease cutting the spring of life' (source: παῦσαι τὴν πηγὴν τῆς ζωῆς προσχῶσᾶν φιλονεικῶν).

problems.quote: Cease cutting the spring of life
problems.source_quote: παῦσαι τὴν πηγὴν τῆς ζωῆς προσχῶσαι φιλονεικῶν
problems.why: προσχῶσαι means 'to dam/block up', not 'cut'; φιλονεικῶν means 'striving/contending'
problems.fix: Cease striving to dam up the spring of life

problems.why: ὠνούμενος means 'winning/purchasing' but context suggests 'cultivating/peddling'; better 'trafficking in falsehood'

edits.old: Cease cutting the spring of life
edits.new: Cease striving to dam up the spring of life

fixed: προσχῶσαι means 'to dam/block up', not 'cut'; φιλονεικῶν means 'striving/contending', so 'Cease cutting the spring of life' misstates the source.
ὠνούμενος means 'buying/purchasing', but in context 'trafficking in falsehood' better captures the sense of cultivating/peddling the lie.

problems.why: ὠνούμενος means 'buying/purchasing', not 'trafficking in' (which implies selling too); he's buying falsehood
problems.ruling: ὠνούμενος = ‘buying’; translation ‘trafficking in’ adds selling nuance

problems.quote: who has heard of an end being disputed, striking fear into those who accomplished it?
problems.source_quote: Τίς ἤκουσε τελευτὴν ἀμφιβαλλομένην καὶ δέος ἐμποιοῦσαν τοῖς ἐργασαμένοις
problems.why: Greek speaks of a death being scattered and terror afflicting the workers; English renders it as an “end being disputed,” changing the meaning.
problems.fix: who has heard a death being scattered and terror afflicting those who did it?
problems.ruling: ἀμφιβαλλομένην means 'disputed/doubted,' but ἐργασαμένοις are those who did it, not 'accomplished it' as workers; δέος ἐμποιοῦσαν is 'striking fear,' but 'end' for τελευτὴν is weak. However, major error is 'those who accomplished it' obscures that ἐργασαμένοις means the killers, and the whole clause structure is garbled.

edits.old: who has heard of an end being disputed, striking fear into those who accomplished it?
edits.new: who has heard of a death being scattered, striking terror into those who accomplished it?

fixed: Changed 'end being disputed' to 'death being scattered' per source τελευτὴν ἀμφιβαλλομένην; 'striking terror' for δέος ἐμποιοῦσαν.
Changed 'trafficking in falsehood' to 'buying falsehood' per source ὠνούμενος (buying).

problems.why: Multiple terms for same group; 'those who dared it' and 'they' in early section may not connect to 'the Jews' later.
problems.fix: Keep 'the Jews' consistent or gloss 'those who dared it'.

problems.quote: Why do you fear the one you have destroyed, O Jew?
problems.why: Shift to second-person address of imagined Jewish opponent is abrupt; no signal who speaks.
problems.fix: Add stage direction: [Addressing an imagined Jewish opponent]

problems.quote: Cease redeeming according to the truth
problems.why: Nonsensical as English; contradicts itself (redeeming according to truth should be good).
problems.fix: Likely 'cease bribing against the truth' or 'cease buying false testimony.'

problems.quote: Cease redeeming according to the truth
problems.why: Probably mistranslation of Greek for 'bribing' or 'hiring false witnesses'; current wording inverts meaning.
problems.fix: Emend to 'Cease bribing against the truth.'

problems.quote: Cease redeeming according to the truth.
problems.why: Does not make sense in context; the surrounding lines say 'cease' + negative actions. 'Redeeming according to the truth' is opaque.
problems.fix: Likely 'cease plotting against the truth' or similar; check the Greek.

problems.quote: If he is a mere man, he does not speak truly when he says, "Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it" (John 2:19).
problems.why: Reader may not realize these are Christ's words quoted from John's Gospel, not the preacher's own claim.
problems.fix: Add 'as Christ himself said' before the quotation.

edits.old: Cease redeeming according to the truth.

fixed: Glossary problem: no change needed; the English uses 'O Jew' and 'you' consistently for the imagined opponent, and the source has Ἰουδαῖε.
Speaker problem: no change needed; the direct address 'O Jew' already signals the shift to the imagined Jewish opponent.
Unreadable problem: the source is παῦσαι λυττῶν κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας, 'cease raging against the truth'; the English 'Cease redeeming according to the truth' is a mistranslation and has been corrected.
Mistranslation problem: corrected to 'Cease raging against the truth' per the source λυττῶν κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας.
Unreadable problem: corrected to 'Cease raging against the truth' per the source.
Speaker problem: no change needed; the quotation is introduced by 'when he says' and the citation to John 2:19 makes clear these are Christ's words.

refereed.why: ὠνούμενος here means 'hiring/purchasing (services)', not 'buying' in a commercial sense; better 'hiring falsehood' or 'procuring falsehood'
refereed.fix: Cease procuring falsehood and stirring up the soldiers
refereed.ruling: ὠνούμενος = ‘being called/named’, not ‘buying’; phrase means ‘stop calling falsehood’, not ‘buying falsehood’.
